  MUNICIPAL SERVICE BUILDING – 633 E. Broadway, 1st Floor, Room 105
  Glendale, CA 91206

  MARCH 02, 2020
  4:00 PM

  1. ROLL CALL

  2. CONSENT ITEMS
  The following are routine and may be acted upon by one motion. Any member of the Commission or the audience requesting separate
  consideration may do so by making such request before motion is proposed.

  a. Approval of the minutes for the February 03, 2020 Meeting

  3. GWP COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS

  4. REPORTS - INFORMATION
  a. Greenhouse Gas Update
  b. Open Mountain Geothermal Renewable Energy Power Purchase Agreement

  5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS (5) Minutes

Welcome to the meeting of the Glendale Water & Power Commission. Meetings are broadcast live on cable channel 6 (GTV6) and rebroadcast throughout the week.

question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact Catalina Lee (818) 548-2107 during regular business hours.
minutes_text:
MINUTES
  MEETING OF THE GLENDALE WATER & POWER COMMISSION

  MUNICIPAL SERVICES BUILDING – 633 E. Broadway, 1st Floor, Room 105
  Glendale, CA 91206

  March 2, 2020
  4:00 PM

1. ROLL CALL
  Present: President Kedikian, Commissioners Avanessian, Carrasco and Lall

2. CONSENT ITEMS
  a. Approval of the February 3, 2020 Meeting Minutes
  The Commission unanimously approved the minutes as published.

3. GWP COMMISSION/ STAFF COMMENTS
  Commissioner Lall and President Kedikian urged residents to vote. Commissioner Lall
  encouraged members of the public to consider applying for the vacant GWP Commission
  position.

4. REPORTS – INFORMATION
  a. Greenhouse Gas Update. Mr. Mark Young, Deputy General Manager, presented a
  report on Greenhouse Gas (GHG) mandates, describing the state regulatory requirement
  and GWP's progress towards achieving the same. Mr. Young stated that we are on target
  to meet the state mandates, and continue to invest in renewable generation and low- and
  zero-carbon assets to maintain compliance. In response to the Commissioners' questions,
  Mr. Young confirmed that the state GHG mandate is not a utility-specific mandate, but a
  statewide requirement and that the baseline was carbon production in 1990. Mr. Young
  stated GWP benchmarks GHG numbers annually, but there is about a one-year lag
  because of the required verification process.

  Mr. Young confirmed that the projections do not take into account the governor's electric
  vehicle mandates, which are expected to increase demand in GWP service territory. He
  stated that there is no link between increasing electric vehicles (EV) and the state's
  Renewables Portfolio Standard. Due to increased EV and electrification of buildings,
  GWP is trying to stay lower in carbon than the regulation requires

  b. Open Mountain Geothermal Power Purchase Agreement. Mr. Young presented the
  Open Mountain Geothermal Power Purchase Agreements. He described the SCPPA
  Renewable Project procurement process and GWP’s participation and due diligence to
  select appropriate projects for Glendale. The Open Mountain projects consist of two
  approximately 25-year geothermal power purchase agreements: Whitegrass, a 3 MW
  existing geothermal project, and Star Peak, a 12.5 MW project which will be constructed in
  the next year. Mr. Young explained why the projects are desirable for Glendale, including
   their high capacity factor (90%), meaning the energy is produced every hour of the day.
  The favorable pricing with no price escalators, especially when considering price reductions
  related to curtailment options and the use of solar generation for auxiliary loads; the
  delivery point, which is a location where GWP holds transmission rights; and the timing of
  the projects, since the second, the larger project will be developed next year. Mr. Young
  stated that the projects would reduce GWP’s carbon footprint by over 52,000 metric tons of
  carbon per year, and the developer, Open Mountain, has over 60 years of clean energy
  experience.

  Mr. Young responded to the Commissioner’s questions. In response to a question about
  the pricing, he compared the pricing of the Open Mountain Geothermal projects to other
  energy sources by referring to the Lazard Levelized Cost of Energy. In response to
  whether GWP can purchase more energy from the project site, Mr. Young noted that we
  have transmission bottlenecks into the Los Angeles Basin, which constrain GWP’s ability to
  bring renewable transmission into Glendale from outside areas.

  Mr. Young explained the GWP power content label, which tells residents where their power
  is coming from. Using the last power content label data from 2018, Mr. Young stated that
  GWP estimates that with the recently-approved Eland Solar and Storage project, an
  estimated 9% increase in GWP’s renewable energy content, and Open Mountain, an
  estimated 11% part of the renewable portfolio, our portfolio could be 56% renewable.

  Mr. Young stated that when this is added to GWP’s other clean assets, which do not count
  as “renewable” under the law, such as considerable hydroelectric energy and nuclear
  power, we estimate our portfolio may be 71% clean in 2022-2023. Mr. Young stated that
  while the numbers are estimated, GWP is doing what we are supposed to do – cleaning up
  our portfolio.

5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  None.

6. AGENDA FORECAST
  The Commissioners reviewed and approved the agenda for the April 2020 meeting, as
  proposed in the Agenda Forecast. President Kedikian inquired whether GWP would be
  bringing an update on the proposed Grayson Repowering. Mr. Young confirmed that GWP
  would do so once further details, including costs and engineering work, are further
  developed.

7. ADJOURNMENT
  Motion to Adjourn:
  Moved by: Commissioner Avanessian
  Seconded by: Commissioner Lall
  Motion Passed.
  The meeting was adjourned at 4:46pm.
